hints: Look carefully at what 1, 2, 3 and 4 are attached to in the diagram. Which ones include a big protein part or a branched carbohydrate chain on the outside?
Remember that proteins have variable amino acid sequences and cell surface carbohydrate chains vary for recognition, while one small lipid in the bilayer has exactly the same structure every time.
walkthrough:
**Identify each labelled structure**

First, let's name what we see. 1 is a peripheral (extrinsic) protein sitting in one layer. 2 is a transmembrane protein with a carbohydrate chain, so a glycoprotein. 3 is a lipid with a carbohydrate chain, so a glycolipid. 4 is the small molecule tucked between phospholipid tails, cholesterol.

Think: protein + carbohydrate = lots of variety for recognition and function.

**Ask which molecules can vary**

Proteins are made of different amino acid sequences, so no two different types of protein (1 and 2) are identical. The carbohydrate chains on glycoproteins (2) and glycolipids (3) also vary in sugars and branching to act as specific cell surface markers.

Only a simple, defined molecule with one fixed structure will always be the same.

**Pick the always identical molecule**

Cholesterol (4) is always the same small lipid molecule wherever it is found in the membrane. It does not have variable sequences like proteins or sugars.

So only 4 is always identical.

options.A: 1 is a protein and 2 and 3 have variable carbohydrate chains, so they differ between different proteins, glycoproteins and glycolipids.
options.B: 1 is a protein with a variable amino acid sequence, so different examples of 1 are not identical, only 4 is.
options.C: 2 is a glycoprotein and 3 is a glycolipid, both have carbohydrate chains that vary in type and branching for cell recognition.
options.D: 4 is cholesterol, a single defined lipid that has the same structure every time it appears in the membrane.
